{"candidate_slot":1,"current_prompt":"You are given a JSON input with two fields: `system_profile` (installed software products with versions) and `advisories` (CVE entries with `id`, `description`, and `affected` version bounds). Identify which supplied advisories apply to the installed system and return ONLY their CVE IDs.

Work through every advisory one at a time and follow this procedure exactly:

STEP 0 — PARSE THE INVENTORY.
Each inventory line is 'product-name version' or 'product-name@version'. The separator between name and version is the LAST whitespace, or '@'. Hyphens, underscores, slashes, dots and spaces inside the name are just separators between name tokens; they do NOT split the product from its version. Examples: 'usta-aybs 1.0.2' -> product tokens {usta, aybs}, version [1,0,2]; 'nozominetworks/guardian@22.6.3.1' -> tokens {nozominetworks, guardian}, version [22,6,3,1]; 'apache-superset 2.1.0.0' -> version [2,1,0,0]. Parse the version as a list of integers. Inventory lines with versions like '20230607' or '31197' are single-segment integer versions.

STEP 1 — PRODUCT MATCHING (for every advisory).
For each advisory, decide whether the affected product appears in the installed inventory. Normalize both names:
- Lowercase everything.
- Split on '-', '_', '/', '.', '@', and spaces; treat all as equivalent separators.
- Compare the resulting sets of tokens ignoring word order and ignoring vendor/organization prefixes when present in only one of the two (e.g. 'usta/aybs' matches 'usta-aybs'; 'Sap Content Server' matches 'sap-content-server'; 'dolibarr_erp/crm' matches 'dolibarr-erp-crm'; 'Blackberry Athoc' matches 'blackberry/athoc'; 'Jetbrains Youtrack' matches 'jetbrains/youtrack'; 'smartrobot' matches 'intumit/smartrobot'; 'weighbridge_automation_software' matches 'uzaybaskul-weighbridge-automation-software'; 'satos_mobile' matches 'satos/satos_mobile').
- A match requires the meaningful product tokens to coincide; a vendor token alone, or a duplicated product token (e.g. 'satos/satos_mobile'), does not block the match, but a genuinely different product name does.
- Multiple advisories in one entry (e.g. 'nozominetworks/cmc ... OR nozominetworks/guardian ...') apply if ANY of the named products is installed.
If the affected product is NOT installed, the advisory is NOT applicable regardless of the description. If it IS installed, proceed to Step 2 and evaluate the version bounds — do not skip this check and do not stop after the product match without concluding.

STEP 2 — VERSION PARSING.
Convert the installed version and every bound in `affected` to lists of integer segments: '5.10.0.1' -> [5,10,0,1]; '20230904' -> [20230904]; '2.2.14' -> [2,2,14]. Compare segment by segment, left to right, padding the shorter list with zeros. Rules:
- Trailing segments that are all zero make the versions EQUAL: '7.15.0' = '7.15'; '11.2.0' = '11.2'; '2.1.0.0' = '2.1.0'; '20230607.0' = '20230607'; '1.0.3.0' = '1.0.3'.
- Any extra trailing segment containing a nonzero digit makes the installed version STRICTLY GREATER: '2.2.14.1' > '2.2.14'; '17.0.3.1' > '17.0.3'; '9.0.18.0.0' — trailing zeros, so it equals '9.0.18'; '22.6.3.1' > '22.6.3'; '9.2.8.1' > '9.2.8'; '7.53.1' > '7.53'; '1.0.10' > '1.0.3'; '1.1.1' > '1.1'.

STEP 3 — BOUND EVALUATION (use ONLY the structured `affected` expression; ignore version claims in the description text).
- 'version < X': applicable only if installed is strictly less than X. '1.0.2' < '1.0.3' is TRUE. '4.10.0.0' < '4.10.0' is FALSE (equal). '11.9.1' < '11.9.0' is FALSE. '3.7.1' < '3.7.2' is TRUE. '9' < '31197' is TRUE. '20230607' < '20230607' is FALSE.
- 'version <= X': applicable if less than or equal after zero-stripping. '2.1.0.0' satisfies '<= 2.1.0'; '19.2' satisfies '<= 19.15'; '7.0.0.0' satisfies '<= 7.0.6' (second alternative 'version = 7.2.0' is false, but the range alternative is true, so the advisory applies).
- 'version = X': applicable only if equal after stripping trailing zero segments. '7.15' = '7.15' TRUE; '2023.1.16597.1' = '2023.1.16597' FALSE; '1.1' = '1.1' TRUE; '11.2.0' = '11.2' TRUE.
- 'version >= X and < Y' (or '<= Y'): installed must satisfy EVERY clause in the range.
- Ranges/alternatives joined by OR: applicable if ANY alternative is satisfied, even if others are false.
- Prose forms like 'versions prior to X are affected' or 'before X' mean 'version < X'.
Do not override the structured bounds with the description; descriptions paraphrase them imprecisely.

STEP 4 — DECIDE.
An advisory is applicable if and only if the product is installed (Step 1) AND the installed version satisfies the affected expression (Step 3). Apply both checks symmetrically:
- Do NOT include an advisory whose product is not installed or whose bound is not satisfied — even if the description sounds relevant or the bound is close.
- Do NOT exclude an advisory merely because of separator, case, word-order, vendor-prefix, or '@' notation differences — if tokens match per Step 1, treat it as installed.
- Do NOT exclude an advisory out of caution or return an empty list when matches exist: if the product is installed and the bound evaluates true, it IS applicable. Default to including every advisory that passes both checks.
- Pay special attention to inclusive bounds: '<= 19.15' applies to '19.2'; '<= 8.6.5' applies to versions in range.
- Pay special attention to exclusive bounds satisfied from below: '< 3.0.0' applies to '2.1.0.1'; '< 1.0.3' applies to '1.0.2'; '< 22.6.3' applies to nothing if installed is '22.6.3.1' (greater) — exclude it.
- A bound like 'version >= 8.5.0 and <= 8.5.4' does NOT apply to '9.2.8.1'; but an OR-alternative covering the installed version does apply.
- Installed versions with a nonzero extra segment (e.g. '22.6.2.1') are GREATER than the bound and do not satisfy '< 22.6.2'.

STEP 5 — OUTPUT.
Return ONLY a JSON object of the form {"applicable_cves":["CVE-...", ...]} listing the IDs of all applicable advisories, each at most once. No markdown, no explanation, no other text. If none apply, return {"applicable_cves":[]}.

Common pitfalls to avoid:
- Declaring a product 'not installed' because of separator, case, word-order, vendor-prefix, or '@' notation differences: normalize names first.
- Treating an installed version with extra nonzero trailing segments (e.g. '2.2.14.1', '22.6.3.1', '9.2.8.1', '1.0.10') as satisfying 'version = X' or '<= X' for the shorter X: it does not; it is strictly greater.
- Treating an installed version with extra zero-only trailing segments (e.g. '7.15.0', '2.1.0.0', '4.10.0.0', '1.0.3.0', '11.9.0.0') as different from the shorter X: they are EQUAL.
- Excluding inclusive bounds: '<= X' applies to X and X.0, X.0.0, and anything below.
- Excluding exclusive bounds satisfied from below: '< 1.0.3' applies to '1.0.2'; '< 5.10.0' does not apply to '5.10.0.0' (equal).
- Letting the description text override the structured bounds or invent a product match.
- Missing applicable advisories: after parsing the inventory, systematically check EVERY advisory whose product tokens match an installed product, and include it whenever the structured bound evaluates true. Never output an empty list without verifying each installed product against every advisory that mentions it.
- Forgetting that multi-product OR expressions apply when any listed product is installed with a satisfying
